Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Chanina challenges a proof involving the impure nazir in the discussion following Acha’s statement. Heilprin treats it as a challenge to Acha and raises a chronology objection.
The narrative names Rabbi Elazar, a Tachlifa with different given-name forms across the adjacent units, Acha son of Ika and Acha bar Yaakov. The bare list supplies no additional relationship.
Rav Pappa and Acha transmit two versions. The text does not say which transmits each version or make Pappa the source of Acha’s view.
The cited unit explicitly names Acha son of Rav Ika speaking to Rav Ashi. Heilprin’s preceding wording mentions Rav Pappa. The note records the digital witness disagreement.
The retrieved Bavli has Adda son of Rav Ika, exactly the form Heilprin reports.
The listed Idi dossier records its own possible Acha correction. Neither pointer licenses treating Adda and Idi as one name.
The notice begins with Acha’s father on 65a. In the continuation other people report the case to Abaye, who replies. The text does not say the father directly addressed Abaye.
